# dbt-plan

> Static analysis that warns about risky DDL changes before `dbt run`. Like `terraform plan`
> for dbt. It compares compiled SQL between two revisions, predicts what DDL dbt would emit,
> and fails CI on destructive changes. Works with any warehouse — Snowflake, BigQuery,
> Redshift, Postgres — because it reads files rather than querying a database.

Install with `pip install dbt-plan`. Requires Python 3.10+. The only runtime dependency is
sqlglot.

It is used the way `terraform plan` is used: before the command that changes the warehouse,
not only in CI afterwards. `dbt-plan check` takes about 0.1 seconds once a baseline exists,
and 0.5 seconds on a 200-model project where every model changed, so it belongs in the edit
loop. The cost is the `dbt compile` that produces its input, which you were running anyway.

The case with no cheap alternative is a macro change: no model file has a diff, yet every
model calling the macro may gain or lose columns. dbt-plan names the affected models and
the columns.

## What it does and does not do

dbt-plan reads `target/compiled/**/*.sql` and `target/manifest.json`, diffs them against a
saved baseline, and reports column additions/removals, materialization changes, changes an
enforced contract will reject, and everything downstream that a dropped column breaks:
models that name it, models that select `*` and lose it without their own file changing,
data tests, and unit tests whose fixtures pin it down. Exit codes drive CI: 0 safe,
1 destructive, 2 warning.

It does not execute SQL, simulate `dbt run`, or connect to a warehouse. It does not judge
`--full-refresh` behavior (a runtime flag), seed/source changes, or pre/post-hook DDL.

Note on credentials: dbt-plan itself never connects, but producing its input requires
`dbt compile`. Under dbt Core that connects, so in CI run compile where credentials already
exist and dbt-plan reads the artifacts; a login with warehouse USAGE is usually enough
unless project macros introspect. Under the Fusion engine `dbt compile` needs no connection
at all, which is what makes a credential-free check on a fork's pull request possible.
Models using introspective macros still fail to compile there, and dbt-plan reports them as
an incomplete compile rather than analysing what is left in silence.

## Risk rules

Safety is decided by materialization crossed with `on_schema_change`:

- table or view, any setting: `CREATE OR REPLACE` — safe
- ephemeral: no physical object — safe
- incremental + `ignore`: no DDL — safe
- incremental + `append_new_columns`: ADD COLUMN only — safe
- incremental + `fail`: build failure on schema drift — warning
- incremental + `sync_all_columns`: ADD and DROP COLUMN — destructive if a column was removed
- snapshot, any setting: review required — warning
- model removed, any setting: destructive
- unrecognized `on_schema_change`: warning
- materialized_view, a dynamic table or a custom materialization with no
  `on_schema_change` set: warning. dbt-plan has no rule for the DDL these emit, and
  materialized views are driven by `on_configuration_change` rather than
  `on_schema_change`. Setting `on_schema_change` explicitly is taken as an assertion
  about how that materialization behaves and the incremental rules above then apply.

When a column cannot be extracted, dbt-plan reports "review required" rather than "safe".
Being noisy is acceptable; missing a destructive change is not.

## Commands

- `dbt-plan run` — compile baseline, compile current, check, in one step
- `dbt-plan snapshot` — save the current compiled state as the baseline
- `dbt-plan check` — compare against the baseline; `--format text|github|json`
- `dbt-plan stats` — summarize the manifest; needs only `dbt parse`, no connection
- `dbt-plan init` — write a `.dbt-plan.yml`
- `dbt-plan ci-setup` — generate `.github/workflows/dbt-plan.yml`
- `dbt-plan agent-setup` — write dbt-plan guidance into the project's `AGENTS.md`

Use `--dialect` to pick the sqlglot dialect (default: snowflake).

In GitHub Actions, `PresentJay/dbt-plan@v1` wraps the whole sequence: it installs
dbt-plan, compiles the base revision and yours, and fails the job on a destructive
verdict. It needs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0`, and whatever credentials
`dbt compile` needs. Keep the `pull_request` trigger -- `pull_request_target` would
expose those credentials to code from any fork.
